newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Tapping sound heard inside Briton's upturned yacht.
newsitem.headline: Tapping sound heard inside Briton's upturned yacht.

text.p: Australian rescue officials said on Thursday that sophisticated microphones had picked up a tapping sound from the capsized yacht of a British solo sailor taking part in a round-the-world yacht race.
They said the sounds from the upturned hull gave them hope Tony Bullimore may still be alive.
The Australian navy frigate HMAS Adelaide was expected to reach Bullimore's yacht in the freezing Southern Ocean waters near Antartica at about 1.30 p.m. (0230 GMT).

A Navy spokesman told Australian Broadcasting Corporation radio that the tapping sounds were picked up just before midnight on Wednesday after an RAAF Orion aircraft dropped a listening device into the water alongside the stricken yacht, the Global Exide Challenger.

"We recorded 90 minutes of return sound from inside the yacht. We hope this is Tony Bullimore tapping inside the yacht, but we temper it by the fact that it could be some debris inside the yacht which has broken free and is tapping against the outside of the hull," the spokesman said.

He said a Seahawk helicopter from HMAS Adelaide was on its way to pick up shipwrecked French yachtsman Thierry Dubois and it was hoped he would be on board the frigate by 9.00 a.m. on Thursday (2200 GMT).

Bullimore, 56, and Dubois, 29, competitors in the Vendee Globe round-the-world race, capsized in wild seas on Sunday after hitting a storm about 900 miles from Antarctica and 1,400 miles from the Australian coast.
Dubois was found by a rescue plane a day later clinging to the upturned hull of his yacht Pour Amnesty International and managed to scramble aboard a life raft dropped from the air.

Bullimore has not been sighted but hopes for his safety were raised on Tuesday when one of his two distress beacons was switched to alert status, an operation that can only be done manually. His yacht is about 60 miles south of Dubois.
HMAS Adelaide's captain, Raydon Gates, said the frigate could only spend 12 hours in the area due to fuel restrictions.
